summary: Fixed a live reopen-after-broker-stop race in S007: decide() could still want a label the broker had already stopped out (its own M1-bar plan lagged the real tick-based fill by one cycle) and would attempt to re-place it with a now-invalid stop, saved only by luck when the broker rejected the order (TRADING_BAD_STOPS). Added StrategyLogger.label_was_opened() and made decide() backfill the close (reason=broker_side_close_detected) the same cycle it notices a previously-opened label missing from broker positions, instead of waiting for the next cycle to notice. Added regression tests covering both the new label_was_opened() method and the end-to-end decide() path.

Extracted the S007 decide()/reconcile logic out of bot/s007_paper.py::live() into a reusable run_cycle_for_account(creds, preset, risk_pct, fixed_lot, use_fixed_lot, magic, logger, ...) function, parameterized instead of hardcoded to bot.s007_config globals; live() now just calls it with the module defaults, so the single-account CLI behaviour is unchanged (verified via --dry-run regression). Rewrote webapp/runner.py for the new broker-agnostic multi-strategy schema (User/Account/AccountStrategy/Strategy) as a coordinator+worker pair: "python -m webapp.runner --strategy S007" loads enabled AccountStrategy rows and spawns one worker subprocess per account (because CTraderAdapter drives its session through a single reactor.run() call -- Twisted reactors cannot be restarted in the same process, so parallel accounts within one tick require one OS process each, not threads/asyncio); a worker runs exactly one cycle for one account_strategy id and exits. Curated events (cycle_start/cycle_end/position_open/position_close/error) now also write to the DB logs table via webapp/schemas/logs.py; full per-tick debug detail (and the label_was_opened/closed dedup state decide() depends on) still goes to per-account utils.trade_logger.StrategyLogger JSONL files under reports/logs/ -- NOT yet safe to drop for containerization, since that dedup state currently only lives in those files (open item). Rewrote webapp/cli.py for the same new schema (init-db/create-user/add-account/add-strategy/link-strategy/enable/disable/list), reusing webapp/schemas/ for validation. S009/Bybit multi-account support deliberately NOT done here: bot/s009_paper.py keeps its ledger state in one shared file for the whole strategy (load_state/save_state), not per (account, strategy), so it would need its own refactor before it could run several accounts in parallel the same way.

Added docs/DEV_PLANS.md, a new dev-plans doc capturing the decided multi-account Docker migration architecture (stateless-tick scheduling, per-strategy job granularity, DB-as-source-of-truth, DB schema decisions, logging split, Alembic migration convention, accounts.yml import mapping) and its current build status, so this is tracked in-repo instead of only in Claude memory. Linked it from README.md's docs/ listing.

Tested the new webapp.runner (coordinator+worker subprocess-per-account) end to end against the real DB-migrated S007/CTRADER account: coordinator found 1 enabled account_strategy row, spawned a worker, worker decrypted DB credentials, ran a full cTrader reconcile cycle, and wrote cycle_start/cycle_end to both the file logger and the DB logs table; account_strategies.status/last_cycle_at updated correctly. Uninstalled the old single-account launchd job (com.anton.algo.s007bot) now that the DB-driven runner path works. Two initial worker runs appeared to hang (55s+ with no output) -- root-caused to stdout full-buffering in a non-TTY subprocess hiding progress, combined with what looks like transient cTrader demo-server slowness, not a code bug: two subsequent clean runs completed in ~7s, matching the old single-account path.
CTraderS007.sync_snapshot(): one-session read-only snapshot of live positions + closing deals, for webapp/sync_positions.py.
details: Added a read-only snapshot call that opens ONE cTrader session and chains, via inlineCallbacks, _load_symbols -> _reconcile_step (ProtoOAReconcileReq) -> _deal_list_step (ProtoOADealListReq, N windows) -> _lot_sizes_step, then stops the reactor. One session because the demo server drops a fresh connection reconnected too soon after the previous one closed, so reconcile and deal-list cannot be two separate calls. Protocol constraints encoded here: (1) a single ProtoOADealListReq may not span more than a week, so the lookback is stitched from <=7-day windows; (2) money int64 fields are scaled by 10^moneyDigits which is PER-MESSAGE, not a constant, so each deal is scaled by its own message's moneyDigits; (3) executionPrice/entryPrice are plain doubles and must NOT be divided by PRICE_SCALE. Returns {'open': [{position_id,label,side,price,sl,tp,volume_lots}], 'deals': [...], 'lot_size': ...}. No orders are placed and nothing is modified at the broker.

summary: Surfaced S007 "ghost" trades: plan_now() now returns reached_tp/n_recovery in context and a new resolved list of positions the engine entered AND resolved (stop/tp/daycap) within the same replayed bars -- these never reach the broker because decide() only places orders for still-open ('eod') positions, so previously they left no trace at all. decide() now logs each first-seen resolved position via a new StrategyLogger.label_was_ghosted()-guarded position(label, "ghost", ...) call. Investigated live 2026-08-05: a B setup formed and resolved before any cycle saw it as open; a historical replay of the events log (2026-08-01 through 2026-08-05) found 2 prior days (08-01, 08-03) with the same pattern -- a scenario detected, n_desired never above 0, no order ever placed -- newly distinguishable from a normal no-signal day now that this is logged.

Fixed a live order-placement bug found while checking today's S007 logs: every cycle since 10:03 today (2026-08-06) rejected with INVALID_REQUEST "Order price ... has more digits than symbol allows" (e.g. 26081.200000000004 for a DE40 symbol that only accepts 2 decimals) -- sl_price/tp_price flow through several float ops (range mid, swing stops) on quotes with up to 5 decimals (PRICE_SCALE), so an unrounded value routinely picks up float noise past the symbol precision. _place_market_step now rounds both to full_symbol.digits (already fetched per cycle for sizing) before sending. No dedicated regression test added yet -- would need the fake-SDK harness in tests/bot/test_check_response.py, which currently fails at collection for an unrelated reason (ctrader_s007 import error), not investigated further here.

Fixed two problems in this test file found while checking today's trading logs. (1) Its autouse _clean_position_log fixture was shutil.rmtree()-ing the REAL reports/logs/S007/positions/ directory before/after every test (not a tmp dir) -- running this file while the live launchd tick (com.anton.algo.s007bot) happened to be mid-cycle deleted all production per-position history and threw a FileNotFoundError in that live cycle (incident 2026-08-06, see decisions-log.md; no data was actually lost, since every position/order event is duplicated into reports/logs/S007/events-<date>.jsonl, untouched by this). Replaced it with monkeypatch.setattr(s007_paper, 'LOG', StrategyLogger("S007TEST", log_root=str(tmp_path))) -- same per-test isolation guarantee, zero risk to real data. (2) The 4 tests mocking plan_now via lambda m1: ... had been broken (TypeError: unexpected keyword argument preset) since the 2026-07-31 run_cycle_for_account refactor added preset=preset to the real call site without updating these mocks; widened the lambda signature to lambda m1, preset=None: .... All 17 tests in the file (plus test_s007_signals.py and test_label_was_closed.py) pass now.

Fixed a second live order-placement bug found today (2026-08-06), right after the price-rounding one: a b-reversal leg is simulated against its own target (tp_A, the opposite range boundary) via _simulate_leg(...tp_A...), but engine.py never stored that per-leg tp on the position dict, and s007_signals.py::plan_now built every wanted positions tp from the single day-level r["tp"] (the PRIMARY B legs target). Live: a reversal BUY went out with the original SELL legs (lower) target attached and cTrader rejected it outright (TRADING_BAD_STOPS: New TP for BUY pending order should be > entry price), repeating every cycle for labels :93/:114/:117 from 11:38 onward, following the same pattern as the earlier :1/:13/:38 sequence. Fix: _simulate_leg now stores tp=tp on every position dict it creates (both the initial entry and pyramided adds); plan_now uses each positions own p["tp"] instead of the shared day-level tp when building wanted/resolved. Verified against the real 2026-06-17 B-stopped/A-reversal-hit-tp historical day (same one used for the ghost-trade fix): the still-open reversal leg now reports tp=24818.666 (rl, correct) instead of 25110.899 (the primary legs tp, which was invalid on the reversal sellside too). Added a regression test asserting a wanted positions tp differs from the day-level context tp and is on the correct side of its own entry.

Generalized webapp/runner.py's strategy dispatch from a hardcoded S007-only check to a STRATEGY_WORKERS registry ({'S007': _worker_s007, 'S009': _worker_s009}), and refactored bot/s009_paper.py so S009 can run multi-account through it: extracted run_cycle_for_account(account_key, creds, state, logger, ...) from run_once()'s body (mirrors bot/s007_paper.py's function of the same name/shape), parameterized by an injectable state store instead of the single global reports/paper_s009/state.json. Added migration 003 (strategy_state table, one JSON blob per account_strategy_id) + webapp/state_store.py::DBStateStore for the DB-driven path, and utils/strategy_state.py::FileStateStore (extracted load_state/save_state) for the unchanged single-account CLI path -- run_once()/--status/--loop/scripts/s009_tick.py keep writing the same file, byte-for-byte, verified via a real --status read after the refactor. _worker_s009 hardcodes broker='off'/allow_mainnet=False deliberately -- enabling real orders through the DB-driven path is a separate future decision, not a side effect. Verified end-to-end against a throwaway copy of the real DB: `webapp.runner --worker --account-strategy-id 3` (Bybit-algo009) correctly wrote a strategy_state row and updated account_strategies.status, with zero broker orders. 55 new+existing tests pass (10 bot, 13 webapp, 32 scripts).

Stopped the S009 test suite from writing into the LIVE paper ledger. run_cycle_for_account() books each closed day via append_ledger(), which resolves LEDGER_FILE/STATE_DIR from bot/s009_paper.py module globals; only one of the eleven tests (test_run_once_uses_the_module_level_state_store) patched them, so every other test that booked a day appended fake rows straight into reports/paper_s009/ledger.csv. Three such rows (day 20001, 2024-10-05, net_ret 0.02, equity 1.02) were found in the live file on 2026-08-08, written after the bot had already booked two real days -- they corrupt the only record of live performance and are exactly what --reconcile reads. Added a module-level autouse fixture _isolate_paper_dirs(tmp_path, monkeypatch) that repoints REPO/STATE_DIR/STATE_FILE/LEDGER_FILE at a temp dir for every test, mirroring the S007 positions-log cleanup fixture (decisions-log 2026-07-21). The three fake rows were removed from the live ledger (backup kept as reports/paper_s009/ledger.csv.bak-20260808-testrows); the two genuine days (2026-08-06 +1.2445%, 2026-08-07 -0.7597%, equity 1.004753) are intact and match state.json. Verified without pytest (unavailable on this bridge VM) by replaying the fixture and the stubbed engine manually and forcing the booking path with last_day = FAKE_DAY - 1: two days booked, both rows landed in the temp ledger, and the real ledger stayed byte-identical (sha256 27dd6a32... before and after). NOT fixed, reported separately: append_ledger() still writes to one global ledger regardless of account_key, so the DB-driven multi-account path would mix every account's equity curve into one file -- the per-account state store has no ledger counterpart.

Fixed a real collision left over from the S009 multi-account refactor: append_ledger() still wrote the module-global LEDGER_FILE regardless of which `state` store was passed to run_cycle_for_account(), so even after state.json was made per-account (DBStateStore), every account's day_pnl rows would still land in the SAME shared reports/paper_s009/ledger.csv -- exactly the collision that refactor was supposed to eliminate. Found because a test run of tests/bot/test_s009_paper.py (before this fix) wrote fake rows into the real live ledger; someone/something added an _isolate_paper_dirs autouse fixture there as a stopgap, which stays. Root-caused and fixed properly: run_cycle_for_account() now takes an explicit ledger_file=None param and only calls append_ledger() when one is given; run_once()'s single-account CLI path passes its own LEDGER_FILE (unchanged behavior, regression-tested), while the DB-driven multi-account path (_worker_s009) deliberately passes none and relies solely on the already-per-account StrategyLogger day_pnl events instead. append_ledger()'s own default was changed from a bound `= LEDGER_FILE` parameter (captured once at def-time, invisible to test monkeypatching) to a None-sentinel resolved fresh on every call. Also added S009 to deployment/schedule.yml (once daily, '5 0 * * *' UTC, not every-minute like S007: run_cycle_for_account has no cheap already-up-to-date short-circuit, so frequent scheduling would hit Bybit's public API for nothing; still broker='off' hardcoded, no orders regardless of cadence). Verified end-to-end against a throwaway migrated copy of the real DB: scripts/scheduler_tick.py correctly dispatched only S009 (not S007) at a simulated 00:05 UTC Monday, wrote strategy_state, zero broker orders.
